newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Jan 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Jan 20.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
LABOUR PLEDGES: NO INCOME TAX PLEDGES
Labour's Shadow Chancellor Gordon Brown today made a manifesto pledge to rule out both a rise in the 23p basic rate of tax and new top rate for higher earners.
EYES ON GREENSPAN AS JAPAN PLUNGES

British equity markets were today set to ignore falling Japanese stocks looking ahead instead to Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's address to congress tomorrow. Experts were predicting that the Footsie would open five points higher in earlier trading.

The Computer Cab radio network is facing series of legal actions from feuding cabbies. The moves are part of an attempt by rebel cabbies to block Com Cab's imminent flotation on the Alternative Investment Market.
LIBERTY JOINS PHONE PENSIONS SALES FORCE

The financial and property concern Liberty International has started dealing in telephone sales of pensions. Through a retail brand called PensionStore the company aims to "offer high quality pensions products either directly or through employers".
SOARAWAY POUND POINTS TO CUT IN HOLIDAY PRICES
Thomson, Britain's biggest tour operator recognises that if sterling and the economy in general continue to rise it may feel obliged to cut prices on summer 1998 holidays.
